findings.title: Do not bypass installer verification when the integration is missing
findings.body: If no Integration row exists for the supplied installation_id, this branch completes the installation without comparing the authenticated GitHub user with the installer. This can happen before the installation webhook is processed or when its delivery fails. The subsequent build_integration fetches the installation using app credentials, which does not establish that the OAuth user has access to it. Consequently, a user supplying another installation's ID can still attach it to their Sentry organization. Fail closed until trusted installer information is available, or verify access using the authenticated user's token.

findings.title: Handle integrations without sender metadata
findings.body: The new check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"], but build_integration only includes sender when it is present in pipeline state. The basic setup flow in this file's tests explicitly creates integration metadata without sender. If such an integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed, attempting to attach it again now raises KeyError and returns a server error rather than a controlled installation failure. Handle missing installer metadata explicitly and obtain trusted verification information before proceeding.

findings.title: Compare immutable GitHub user IDs instead of logins
findings.body: Installer identity is checked using the login saved in webhook metadata and the current OAuth user's login. GitHub usernames can change and old usernames can be claimed by another account. A legitimate installer who renames their account will therefore be rejected, while a different account claiming the old username can pass this check for an unlinked installation. Store and compare the immutable GitHub user ID returned by both the webhook sender and the authenticated-user endpoint.
